ENSO and the PDO are two important climate modes affecting precipitation/streamflow across China and that the combined effect of ENSO with PDO on precipitation/streamflow is opposite in northern China to that in southern China.

the impacts of ENSO/PDCO on precipitation/streamflow in China have regional and seasonal differences, and that the responses of precipitation and streamflow to the combined influence of the ENSO and the PDO are different in northern and southern China.

the impacts of ENSO/PD on precipitation and streamflows in China during the period 1900 to 2000 and provides an important basis for water resources management and planning in China.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the precipitation/streamflow in the Pearl River and Yangtze River basins are more significantly influenced than the precipitation/streamflow of other basins in the whole country, and the precipitation/streamflow are relatively more significant during the warm phase of PDO than during the cool phase of PDO.
ENSO has greater influence than PDO on precipitation/streamflow in the majority of the China.

El Nino and PDO warm phases are generally associated with a decrease in precipitation/streamflow in most of China, except in the Songhua and Yellow river basins, while La Nina and PDO cool phases are associated with a general increase in precipitation/streamflow, with the most significant impact on the Yangtze and Pearl River basins.

the ENSO/PDC signals can be detected in the precipitation/streamflow series over China during the last one century.

the impacts of ENSO/PD0 on precipitation/streamflow vary in space and time, and the combined influence is more complicated and should be considered in water resources management.
